summary:
Turn 2 resolved the active Candidate's discriminator on sources and clarified the map accordingly.

State on entry. The first product was accepted as audit spec v1: core_overview usable for both core relationships, 7 activities, 16 behaviors, 7 facts, 7 surfaces, and Candidate d8fd7f58 (the handlePreAccept wrong-slot write) active in pending_work with next_objective investigate_and_refocus.

What was decided. The Candidate asked whether any legal history reaches handlePreAccept's Status >= ACCEPTED branch with Cmds == nil (the premise for writing a command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance]). Enumerating every writer of Instance.Cmds and Instance.Status in the snapshot answers it: no. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also installs commands in the same handler (handlePreAccept stores the received command, handlePreAcceptReply/handleTryPreAcceptReply/handleAcceptReply copy lb.cmds, handleCommit copies commit.Command); a commit command cannot arrive as nil because Marshal writes a zero-length prefix and Unmarshal allocates a non-nil empty slice; and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE. The line 809 branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance: the two sourced discrepancies currently compensate instead of composing into a defect. Submitted action=explained with that protective mechanism, scoped sourced counterevidence, and a refinement of the Candidate's unknowns rather than of its requirement.

Map updates (same product). B3 now records the sourced protection and the answered unknown; B5 records precisely what an acceptor stores and the separated premise; core_overview's first open detail is replaced by the sourced conditional relationship (wrong-slot index retained, branch premise not produced, accept-status premise separated). The other six open details are untouched.

Separated lead. Whether the accept phase must record ACCEPTED is a different responsibility: handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard, findPreAcceptConflicts' already-ACCEPTED shortcut and handlePrepareReply sub-case 2 all presuppose an accepted status observable on a replica that never led the instance, and handlePrepareReply's value selection may adopt a status-NONE, command-less reply at the highest vbal instead of an equal-vbal reply that carries the value. That is carried in feedback as the next discriminator; no formal execution was submitted this turn, and no accepted requirement, premise or history was weakened.
